---
title: "Who Wants to Be a Macro Millionaire?"
subtitle: "15 questions on AD, AS, and business cycles — Ch. 15"
toc: false
---

Answer each question to climb the prize ladder. Three lifelines, two safe floors, one shot at a million.

```{=html}
<style>
  .mm-wrap { font-family: "Inter", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; }
  .mm-board {
    background: linear-gradient(160deg, #07101f 0%, #0d1e40 55%, #091526 100%);
    border-radius: 12px;
    padding: 1.4rem 1.6rem;
    color: #e8eaf6;
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 170px;
    gap: 1.4rem;
    min-height: 440px;
    box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
  }
  .mm-play { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.9rem; }

  /* Status bar */
  .mm-status {
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between;
    font-size: 0.72rem; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace;
    letter-spacing: 0.07em; text-transform: uppercase;
    color: #7ecfee; padding-bottom: 0.5rem;
    border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
  }

  /* Lifelines */
  .mm-lifelines { display: flex; gap: 0.45rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .mm-ll {
    background: rgba(30,50,120,0.7); border: 1.5px solid #3a5aaa;
    border-radius: 20px; padding: 0.3rem 0.75rem;
    color: #a8c4ff; font-size: 0.75rem; cursor: pointer;
    font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace;
    transition: border-color 0.15s, color 0.15s;
    white-space: nowrap;
  }
  .mm-ll:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: #7bd3f6; color: #7bd3f6; }
  .mm-ll:disabled { opacity: 0.28; cursor: default; text-decoration: line-through; }

  /* Question */
  .mm-qnum {
    font-size: 0.7rem; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace;
    letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #90b4d8;
  }
  .mm-qtext { font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.65; color: #dde4f0; min-height: 3.5rem; }

  /* Choices */
  .mm-choices { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 0.55rem; }
  .mm-choice {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #12235a 0%, #0b1840 100%);
    border: 1.5px solid #2e4090; border-radius: 28px;
    padding: 0.58rem 0.9rem; color: #d0daef; cursor: pointer;
    font-size: 0.86rem; line-height: 1.4; text-align: left;
    display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 0.5rem;
    transition: border-color 0.15s, color 0.15s, background 0.15s;
  }
  .mm-choice:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: #ffd700; color: #ffd700; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1e3580, #12235a); }
  .mm-choice:disabled { cursor: default; }
  .mm-choice.eliminated { opacity: 0.12; }
  .mm-choice.selected { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4a3300, #6a4c00); border-color: #ffd700; color: #ffe066; }
  .mm-choice.confirming { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #5a3f00, #7a5500); border-color: #ffaa00; color: #ffdd80; animation: mm-pulse 0.45s ease-in-out 4; }
  .mm-choice.correct { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0a3d00, #145200); border-color: #4caf50; color: #b9f6ca; }
  .mm-choice.wrong   { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4a0000, #660000); border-color: #f44336; color: #ffcdd2; }
  @keyframes mm-pulse { 0%,100%{transform:scale(1)} 50%{transform:scale(1.015)} }
  .mm-cletter {
    display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
    width: 1.55rem; height: 1.55rem; border-radius: 50%;
    border: 1.5px solid currentColor; font-size: 0.72rem;
    font-weight: 700; flex-shrink: 0;
    font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace;
  }

  /* Feedback / hint panel */
  .mm-panel {
    background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.09);
    border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem;
    font-size: 0.83rem; color: #b0bcd8; line-height: 1.6;
    animation: mf-fade-in 0.3s ease-out;
  }
  .mm-panel strong { color: #dde4f0; }

  /* Poll bars */
  .mm-poll { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.35rem; }
  .mm-poll-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.78rem; color: #c0cce6; }
  .mm-poll-lbl { width: 1rem; font-family: monospace; font-weight: 700; color: #ffd700; flex-shrink: 0; }
  .mm-poll-bg { flex: 1; height: 14px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.07); border-radius: 3px; overflow: hidden; }
  .mm-poll-fill { height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #1565c0, #42a5f5); border-radius: 3px; transition: width 0.7s ease; }
  .mm-poll-pct { width: 2.8rem; text-align: right; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.73rem; color: #8a9fc0; }

  /* Action controls */
  .mm-controls { display: flex; gap: 0.45rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .mm-btn {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #b8860b, #cfa016);
    border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.42rem 0.95rem;
    color: #07101f; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.8rem; cursor: pointer;
    transition: filter 0.15s, transform 0.1s;
    font-family: "Inter", -apple-system, sans-serif;
  }
  .mm-btn:hover:not(:disabled) { filter: brightness(1.15); transform: translateY(-1px); }
  .mm-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.35; cursor: default; }
  .mm-btn.sec {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #162060, #0d1840);
    border: 1px solid #304090; color: #90a8d8;
  }

  /* Prize ladder */
  .mm-ladder { display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; gap: 2px; padding-top: 0.15rem; }
  .mm-rung {
    display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center;
    padding: 3px 8px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.7rem;
    font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace;
    color: #6a7a9a; transition: all 0.3s;
  }
  .mm-rung.safe { color: #5bc8e8; }
  .mm-rung.passed { color: #4caf50; }
  .mm-rung.current { background: linear-gradient(90deg, #8a6500, #cfa016); color: #07101f; font-weight: 700; }

  /* Splash / end screens */
  .mm-splash { text-align: center; padding: 1.5rem 0.5rem; }
  .mm-splash h3 { font-size: 1.6rem; color: #ffd700; text-shadow: 0 0 18px rgba(255,215,0,0.4); margin: 0 0 0.5rem; }
  .mm-splash p { color: #8090b0; font-size: 0.88rem; max-width: 380px; margin: 0 auto 1.2rem; line-height: 1.65; }
  .mm-big-prize { font-size: 2.2rem; font-weight: 900; color: #ffd700; text-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(255,215,0,0.45); margin: 0.4rem 0; }
  .mm-lifeline-info { font-size: 0.77rem; color: #5a7090; margin-bottom: 1.2rem; }

  @media (max-width: 600px) {
    .mm-board { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    .mm-ladder { flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px; padding-top: 0; }
    .mm-rung { font-size: 0.62rem; padding: 2px 6px; }
    .mm-choices { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  }
</style>

<div class="mm-wrap">
  <div class="mm-board">
    <div class="mm-play" id="mm-play"></div>
    <div class="mm-ladder" id="mm-ladder"></div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  const PRIZES = ["$100","$200","$300","$500","$1,000","$2,000","$4,000","$8,000","$16,000","$32,000","$64,000","$125,000","$250,000","$500,000","$1,000,000"];
  const SAFE = new Set([4, 9]);   // $1,000 and $32,000 (0-based)
  const LETTERS = ["A","B","C","D"];

  // 15 questions from Ch. 15 (AD-AS, business cycles, monetary policy)
  const QS = [
    {
      topic: "Business cycles",
      q: "During recessions, unemployment typically ___",
      ch: ["falls slightly before the recession ends",
           "stays flat, because wage floors prevent most job losses",
           "rises substantially; as the recession ends it declines gradually",
           "rises and permanently stays above its pre-recession level"],
      ans: 2,
      why: "Unemployment jumps sharply during recessions and then heals slowly. Labor markets are sticky on the way back up.",
      hint: "The professor says: think about which direction unemployment moves when output falls — then ask whether it snaps back immediately once output recovers.",
      poll: [4, 3, 88, 5],
      kill: [0, 3]   // 50-50 eliminates these two wrong-answer indices
    },
    {
      topic: "AD shifts",
      q: "A stock market boom makes households feel wealthier. In the AD-AS diagram, the direct effect is ___",
      ch: ["aggregate demand shifts right",
           "short-run aggregate supply shifts right",
           "long-run aggregate supply shifts right",
           "aggregate demand shifts left"],
      ans: 0,
      why: "Higher household wealth raises consumption. That is a shift of aggregate demand, not a movement along it.",
      hint: "The professor says: higher wealth → higher consumption spending → what happens to total planned expenditure at each price level?",
      poll: [80, 7, 5, 8],
      kill: [1, 3]
    },
    {
      topic: "AD shifts",
      q: "When government purchases increase, the initial effect in the AD-AS model is ___",
      ch: ["AD shifts left, because higher spending crowds out private investment immediately",
           "SRAS shifts right, because firms now have guaranteed government sales",
           "LRAS shifts right, because public capital raises long-run potential output",
           "AD shifts right"],
      ans: 3,
      why: "Government purchases are a direct component of aggregate demand (C + I + G + NX). More G shifts AD right regardless of what happens later.",
      hint: "The professor says: G is one of the four components of aggregate demand. Adding more of a component shifts the whole curve.",
      poll: [5, 4, 8, 83],
      kill: [0, 2]
    },
    {
      topic: "Classical theory",
      q: "David Hume's observation that gold discoveries expanded the money supply taught economists that ___",
      ch: ["prices rose immediately with no temporary effect on output",
           "the LRAS curve shifted right as gold expanded productive capacity",
           "output fell because gold crowded out real investment",
           "it took time for prices to rise; in the meantime output was higher"],
      ans: 3,
      why: "Hume's point was that prices do not adjust instantly. A money expansion can temporarily raise spending and output before the price level fully catches up.",
      hint: "The professor says: Hume is illustrating that money is non-neutral in the short run even if it is neutral in the long run.",
      poll: [6, 5, 4, 85],
      kill: [0, 2]
    },
    {
      topic: "Aggregate demand",
      q: "Aggregate demand equals C + I + G + NX, so it includes ___",
      ch: ["both domestic government purchases and foreign demand for domestic goods",
           "only domestic private consumption and investment",
           "the quantity of goods firms want to produce at each price level",
           "real GDP minus transfers and taxes"],
      ans: 0,
      why: "Aggregate demand is total planned spending. That includes government purchases (G) and foreign purchases of domestic goods through net exports (NX).",
      hint: "The professor says: look at the NX term — exports represent foreigners buying our goods, so foreign demand is in there.",
      poll: [79, 8, 7, 6],
      kill: [1, 3]
    },
    {
      topic: "AD slope",
      q: "When the price level rises, this is shown in the AD-AS diagram as ___",
      ch: ["a rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve",
           "a rightward shift of the short-run aggregate supply curve",
           "a movement to the left along a given aggregate demand curve",
           "a leftward shift of short-run aggregate supply"],
      ans: 2,
      why: "Changing the price level moves the economy along the AD curve. A higher price level means lower quantity demanded — a leftward movement along AD, not a shift.",
      hint: "The professor says: distinguish between what shifts a curve (something other than the price level) versus what moves you along it (a price-level change).",
      poll: [9, 6, 74, 11],
      kill: [0, 3]
    },
    {
      topic: "AD slope",
      q: "The wealth effect, interest-rate effect, and exchange-rate effect are all explanations for ___",
      ch: ["why LRAS is vertical at natural output",
           "why SRAS slopes upward in the short run",
           "the downward slope of the aggregate demand curve",
           "why the money multiplier exceeds 1"],
      ans: 2,
      why: "Each effect gives a reason why a higher price level reduces the quantity of goods and services demanded — together they explain why AD slopes downward.",
      hint: "The professor says: each of these three effects links a higher price level to lower spending. That is a story about the slope of AD.",
      poll: [11, 8, 74, 7],
      kill: [0, 3]
    },
    {
      topic: "Long-run AS",
      q: "The long-run aggregate supply curve is vertical because, in the long run ___",
      ch: ["the price level is fixed by central-bank policy",
           "monetary expansion always raises prices and output in exactly equal proportion",
           "wages are perfectly flexible so employment always equals its natural rate",
           "output is determined by resources and technology, not by the price level"],
      ans: 3,
      why: "LRAS is vertical because long-run output is determined by labor, capital, natural resources, and technology — real factors, not the price level. That is the classical dichotomy.",
      hint: "The professor says: in the long run, what determines how much an economy can produce? It is not the price level — prices just determine the nominal value.",
      poll: [8, 6, 18, 68],
      kill: [0, 1]
    },
    {
      topic: "Short-run AS",
      q: "An increase in the expected price level shifts short-run aggregate supply ___",
      ch: ["right, because firms expect higher revenue and expand hiring",
           "right for SRAS and left for LRAS simultaneously",
           "left only if the actual price level also rises",
           "left; and an increase in the actual price level does not shift SRAS"],
      ans: 3,
      why: "Expected prices shift SRAS because they change wage-setting and input-cost expectations. Actual price-level changes move the economy along SRAS — they do not shift it.",
      hint: "The professor says: sticky-wage theory says firms set wages based on expected prices. Raising expectations raises costs at each output level — that shifts SRAS left.",
      poll: [14, 7, 10, 69],
      kill: [0, 2]
    },
    {
      topic: "SR-LR adjustment",
      q: "Starting at long-run equilibrium, aggregate demand falls. After full long-run adjustment, the economy reaches ___",
      ch: ["a permanently lower output with a lower price level",
           "the original output with an unchanged price level",
           "the original long-run output level but at a lower price level",
           "higher output because SRAS shifts right in response"],
      ans: 2,
      why: "After an AD fall, output is below natural output in the short run. Over time wages and expected prices fall, SRAS shifts right, and output returns to natural. The price level ends up lower.",
      hint: "The professor says: ask what happens to wages when the economy is stuck below potential for a long time — and what that does to SRAS.",
      poll: [18, 9, 61, 12],
      kill: [0, 3]
    },
    {
      topic: "Short-run AS / sticky wages",
      q: "The sticky-wage theory says that when the actual price level is lower than expected ___",
      ch: ["firms lower nominal wages immediately, restoring profit margins",
           "workers accept real wage cuts to keep their jobs, so employment holds",
           "output rises because lower prices expand real consumer spending",
           "production becomes less profitable and employment falls"],
      ans: 3,
      why: "If prices fall below expectations while nominal wages are fixed, real wages are too high relative to output prices. Production is less profitable, so firms reduce employment.",
      hint: "The professor says: wages are set in advance based on expected prices. If actual prices come in lower, are workers costing more or less relative to output value?",
      poll: [10, 12, 8, 70],
      kill: [0, 2]
    },
    {
      topic: "SRAS vs LRAS",
      q: "Which of the following shifts short-run aggregate supply right but does NOT shift long-run aggregate supply right?",
      ch: ["an increase in the physical capital stock",
           "a decrease in the expected price level",
           "an increase in immigration that expands the labor force",
           "a breakthrough in production technology"],
      ans: 1,
      why: "Lower expected prices reduce wage-setting and input-cost expectations, shifting SRAS right. They do not change the economy's productive capacity, so LRAS is unaffected.",
      hint: "The professor says: think about what each option does to long-run productive capacity. Expected prices affect costs, not capacity.",
      poll: [20, 46, 16, 18],
      kill: [0, 3]
    },
    {
      topic: "Misperceptions theory",
      q: "Under the misperceptions theory, a firm expected 4% inflation but actual inflation is only 2%. The firm perceives that the relative price of its output has ___",
      ch: ["risen, so it increases production",
           "stayed the same; it ignores overall inflation",
           "risen because its input costs fell relative to its output price",
           "decreased, so it decreases production"],
      ans: 3,
      why: "Actual inflation below expected inflation makes the firm think overall prices are lower than its product price. It infers its relative price has fallen and cuts output.",
      hint: "The professor says: the firm cannot tell general price changes from relative price changes. Lower-than-expected inflation looks like a price drop specific to its product.",
      poll: [9, 5, 8, 78],
      kill: [0, 1]
    },
    {
      topic: "Monetary neutrality",
      q: "In the AD-AS model, an increase in the money supply leads, in the long run, to ___",
      ch: ["higher real GDP and a higher price level",
           "higher real GDP but no change in the price level",
           "a higher price level but no change in real GDP",
           "no change in either the price level or real GDP"],
      ans: 2,
      why: "In the long run, money is neutral. More money raises AD and the price level, but real GDP returns to natural output. Classical dichotomy holds.",
      hint: "The professor says: LRAS is vertical. A rightward AD shift moves equilibrium up the vertical LRAS — output ends up the same, only the price level changes.",
      poll: [14, 5, 73, 8],
      kill: [0, 1]
    },
    {
      topic: "SR-LR adjustment",
      q: "The U.S. has had both rising prices and rising real GDP since World War II. To explain this simultaneously in the AD-AS framework ___",
      ch: ["only aggregate demand shifting right is required",
           "only long-run aggregate supply shifting right is required",
           "both AD and LRAS must shift right, and AD must shift farther than LRAS",
           "short-run aggregate supply shifting right while AD remains fixed is sufficient"],
      ans: 2,
      why: "Real GDP growth requires LRAS to shift right (more productive capacity). Rising prices require AD to shift right even farther than LRAS so the equilibrium price level drifts up.",
      hint: "The professor says: draw this out. If both AD and LRAS shift right by the same amount, the price level is unchanged. To get rising prices, AD must outrun LRAS.",
      poll: [16, 8, 67, 9],
      kill: [0, 3]
    }
  ];

  // ── State ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  let state = "splash";   // splash | question | confirming | revealed | gameover | walkaway | win
  let qi = 0;             // current question index
  let selected = -1;      // chosen answer index (-1 = none)
  let eliminated = new Set();
  let llUsed = { half: false, prof: false, poll: false };
  let showHint = false;
  let showPoll = false;
  let guaranteed = 0;     // index of highest safe floor passed

  // ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  const play  = () => document.getElementById("mm-play");
  const ladderEl = () => document.getElementById("mm-ladder");

  function esc(s) {
    return String(s).replace(/&/g,"&amp;").replace(/</g,"&lt;").replace(/>/g,"&gt;");
  }

  function renderLadder() {
    ladderEl().innerHTML = PRIZES.map((p, i) => {
      let cls = "mm-rung";
      if (i === qi && (state === "question" || state === "confirming" || state === "revealed")) cls += " current";
      else if (SAFE.has(i)) cls += " safe";
      else if (i < qi) cls += " passed";
      const num = i + 1;
      return `<div class="${cls}"><span>${num}</span><span>${p}</span></div>`;
    }).join("");
  }

  function choiceClass(i) {
    if (eliminated.has(i)) return "mm-choice eliminated";
    if (state === "confirming" && i === selected) return "mm-choice confirming";
    if (state === "revealed") {
      if (i === QS[qi].ans) return "mm-choice correct";
      if (i === selected && i !== QS[qi].ans) return "mm-choice wrong";
    }
    if (state === "question" && i === selected) return "mm-choice selected";
    return "mm-choice";
  }

  function choiceDisabled(i) {
    return state !== "question" || eliminated.has(i);
  }

  function pollHTML(q) {
    return `<div class="mm-poll">` +
      LETTERS.map((l, i) => {
        if (eliminated.has(i)) return "";
        const pct = q.poll[i];
        return `<div class="mm-poll-row">
          <span class="mm-poll-lbl">${l}</span>
          <div class="mm-poll-bg"><div class="mm-poll-fill" style="width:${pct}%"></div></div>
          <span class="mm-poll-pct">${pct}%</span>
        </div>`;
      }).join("") +
    `</div>`;
  }

  // ── Screens ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function renderSplash() {
    play().innerHTML = `
      <div class="mm-splash">
        <h3>Who Wants to Be a Macro Millionaire?</h3>
        <p>15 questions on aggregate demand, aggregate supply, and business cycles from Ch.&nbsp;15. Two safe floors — $1,000 and $32,000. Three lifelines: 50:50, Phone a Professor, and Ask the Class.</p>
        <div class="mm-lifeline-info">50:50 &nbsp;·&nbsp; Phone a Professor &nbsp;·&nbsp; Ask the Class</div>
        <div class="mm-controls" style="justify-content:center">
          <button class="mm-btn" id="mm-start">Start the game</button>
        </div>
      </div>`;
    ladderEl().innerHTML = "";
    document.getElementById("mm-start").onclick = startGame;
  }

  function renderQuestion() {
    const q = QS[qi];
    const choicesHTML = q.ch.map((c, i) =>
      `<button class="${choiceClass(i)}"
              data-choice="${i}"
              ${choiceDisabled(i) ? "disabled" : ""}>
        <span class="mm-cletter">${LETTERS[i]}</span>${esc(c)}
      </button>`
    ).join("");

    const confirmBtn = selected >= 0 && state === "question"
      ? `<button class="mm-btn" id="mm-confirm">Final answer</button>` : "";
    const walkBtn = `<button class="mm-btn sec" id="mm-walk">Walk away${guaranteed > 0 ? " (keep "+PRIZES[guaranteed-1]+")" : ""}</button>`;
    const nextBtn = state === "revealed"
      ? `<button class="mm-btn" id="mm-next">${qi === QS.length - 1 ? "Claim your million!" : "Next question"}</button>` : "";

    let panelHTML = "";
    if (state === "confirming") {
      panelHTML = `<div class="mm-panel"><strong>Is that your final answer?</strong> You selected <strong>${LETTERS[selected]}. ${esc(q.ch[selected])}</strong>. Lock it in or pick again.</div>`;
    } else if (state === "revealed") {
      const correct = selected === q.ans;
      panelHTML = `<div class="mm-panel">
        <strong>${correct ? "Correct!" : `Wrong. The answer was ${LETTERS[q.ans]}. ${esc(q.ch[q.ans])}`}</strong><br>
        ${esc(q.why)}
      </div>`;
    } else {
      if (showHint)  panelHTML = `<div class="mm-panel"><strong>📞 Professor:</strong> ${esc(q.hint)}</div>`;
      if (showPoll)  panelHTML += `<div class="mm-panel"><strong>📊 Ask the Class:</strong><br>${pollHTML(q)}</div>`;
    }

    play().innerHTML = `
      <div class="mm-status">
        <span>Question ${qi + 1} of ${QS.length}</span>
        <span style="color:#b0c0e0">${esc(q.topic)}</span>
        <span>${PRIZES[qi]}</span>
      </div>
      <div class="mm-lifelines">
        <button class="mm-ll" id="ll-half" ${llUsed.half || state !== "question" ? "disabled" : ""}>50:50</button>
        <button class="mm-ll" id="ll-prof" ${llUsed.prof || state !== "question" ? "disabled" : ""}>📞 Professor</button>
        <button class="mm-ll" id="ll-poll" ${llUsed.poll || state !== "question" ? "disabled" : ""}>📊 Ask the Class</button>
      </div>
      <div class="mm-qtext">${esc(q.q)}</div>
      <div class="mm-choices">${choicesHTML}</div>
      ${panelHTML}
      <div class="mm-controls">
        ${state === "confirming"
          ? `<button class="mm-btn" id="mm-lock">Yes, final answer</button>
             <button class="mm-btn sec" id="mm-unselect">Go back</button>`
          : confirmBtn + (state === "question" ? walkBtn : "") + nextBtn}
      </div>`;

    // Wire lifelines
    if (!llUsed.half) document.getElementById("ll-half")?.addEventListener("click", useHalf);
    if (!llUsed.prof) document.getElementById("ll-prof")?.addEventListener("click", useProf);
    if (!llUsed.poll) document.getElementById("ll-poll")?.addEventListener("click", usePoll);

    // Wire choice buttons
    play().querySelectorAll("[data-choice]").forEach(btn => {
      btn.addEventListener("click", () => selectChoice(Number(btn.dataset.choice)));
    });

    document.getElementById("mm-confirm")?.addEventListener("click", confirmAnswer);
    document.getElementById("mm-lock")?.addEventListener("click", lockAnswer);
    document.getElementById("mm-unselect")?.addEventListener("click", () => { selected = -1; render(); });
    document.getElementById("mm-walk")?.addEventListener("click", walkAway);
    document.getElementById("mm-next")?.addEventListener("click", nextQuestion);

    renderLadder();
  }

  function renderGameOver() {
    const safeWin = guaranteed > 0 ? PRIZES[guaranteed - 1] : "$0";
    play().innerHTML = `
      <div class="mm-splash">
        <h3 style="color:#f44336">Eliminated!</h3>
        <p>You answered question ${qi + 1} incorrectly. The correct answer was <strong>${LETTERS[QS[qi].ans]}. ${esc(QS[qi].ch[QS[qi].ans])}</strong>.</p>
        <p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:#607090">${esc(QS[qi].why)}</p>
        <div class="mm-big-prize" style="color:#5bc8e8">${safeWin}</div>
        <p style="color:#607090">You leave with your safe-floor winnings.</p>
        <div class="mm-controls" style="justify-content:center">
          <button class="mm-btn" id="mm-restart">Play again</button>
        </div>
      </div>`;
    renderLadder();
    document.getElementById("mm-restart").onclick = startGame;
  }

  function renderWalkAway() {
    const walked = PRIZES[qi];
    play().innerHTML = `
      <div class="mm-splash">
        <h3 style="color:#5bc8e8">You walked away!</h3>
        <div class="mm-big-prize">${walked}</div>
        <p>You quit at question ${qi + 1} and keep <strong>${walked}</strong>. Bold play — question ${qi + 1} was worth ${PRIZES[qi]}.</p>
        <div class="mm-controls" style="justify-content:center">
          <button class="mm-btn" id="mm-restart">Play again</button>
        </div>
      </div>`;
    renderLadder();
    document.getElementById("mm-restart").onclick = startGame;
  }

  function renderWin() {
    play().innerHTML = `
      <div class="mm-splash">
        <h3>Macro Millionaire!</h3>
        <div class="mm-big-prize">$1,000,000</div>
        <p>You answered all 15 questions correctly. You know your AD-AS inside out.</p>
        <div class="mm-controls" style="justify-content:center">
          <button class="mm-btn" id="mm-restart">Play again</button>
        </div>
      </div>`;
    renderLadder();
    document.getElementById("mm-restart").onclick = startGame;
  }

  // ── Render dispatcher ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function render() {
    if (state === "splash")    renderSplash();
    else if (state === "gameover") renderGameOver();
    else if (state === "walkaway") renderWalkAway();
    else if (state === "win")      renderWin();
    else renderQuestion();
  }

  // ── Actions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function startGame() {
    qi = 0; selected = -1; eliminated = new Set();
    llUsed = { half: false, prof: false, poll: false };
    showHint = false; showPoll = false; guaranteed = 0;
    state = "question";
    render();
  }

  function selectChoice(i) {
    if (state !== "question" || eliminated.has(i)) return;
    selected = i;
    render();
  }

  function confirmAnswer() {
    if (selected < 0) return;
    state = "confirming";
    render();
  }

  function lockAnswer() {
    const correct = selected === QS[qi].ans;
    state = "revealed";
    render();
    if (!correct) { setTimeout(() => { state = "gameover"; render(); }, 2200); }
  }

  function nextQuestion() {
    // Update safe floor
    if (SAFE.has(qi)) guaranteed = qi + 1;
    qi += 1;
    if (qi >= QS.length) { state = "win"; render(); return; }
    selected = -1; eliminated = new Set();
    showHint = false; showPoll = false;
    state = "question";
    render();
  }

  function walkAway() {
    state = "walkaway";
    render();
  }

  function useHalf() {
    if (llUsed.half) return;
    llUsed.half = true;
    showHint = false; showPoll = false;
    // eliminate the two wrong answers listed in the question's kill array
    QS[qi].kill.forEach(i => eliminated.add(i));
    // if somehow selected choice got eliminated, clear it
    if (eliminated.has(selected)) selected = -1;
    render();
  }

  function useProf() {
    if (llUsed.prof) return;
    llUsed.prof = true;
    showHint = true;
    render();
  }

  function usePoll() {
    if (llUsed.poll) return;
    llUsed.poll = true;
    showPoll = true;
    render();
  }

  // ── Boot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  render();
})();
</script>
```
